The numbers 1, 2, ..., 2100 are written on a board. Every second, Mark takes two numbers on the board, \( a \) and \( b \), erases them, and replaces them with \( \gcd(a, b) \) and \( \operatorname{lcm}(a, b) \). Mark stops once any move he makes will not change the numbers written on the board. Compute the number of divisors of the 2026th smallest positive integer written on the board when he finishes.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

Let \(v_p(n)\) denote the exponent of prime \(p\) in \(n\).

When Mark replaces \(a,b\) with \(\gcd(a,b),\operatorname{lcm}(a,b)\), for each prime \(p\), the two \(p\)-exponents \(v_p(a),v_p(b)\) are replaced by

\[
\min(v_p(a),v_p(b)),\quad \max(v_p(a),v_p(b)).
\]

So for every prime \(p\), the multiset of \(p\)-exponents on the board is invariant.

At the stopping time, no move can change the board. If two distinct numbers were incomparable under divisibility, then their gcd and lcm would both be different from the original two numbers, so that move would change the board. Hence the final board is a chain under divisibility.

List the final board as

\[
c_1\le c_2\le \cdots \le c_{2100}.
\]

Since it is a divisibility chain, \(c_i\mid c_j\) for \(i<j\). Thus for each prime \(p\), the sequence \(v_p(c_1),v_p(c_2),\dots,v_p(c_{2100})\) is nondecreasing. Because the multiset of \(p\)-exponents is unchanged from the beginning, \(v_p(c_i)\) must be the \(i\)-th smallest value among

\[
v_p(1),v_p(2),\dots,v_p(2100).
\]

We need \(c_{2026}\). This is the \(75\)-th largest entry, since

\[
2100-2026+1=75.
\]

Therefore \(v_p(c_{2026})\) is the \(75\)-th largest \(p\)-exponent among \(1,2,\dots,2100\). Equivalently,

\[
v_p(c_{2026})=\max\left\{k\ge 0:\left\lfloor \frac{2100}{p^k}\right\rfloor\ge 75\right\}.
\]

Now compute:

- For \(p=2\):
  \[
  \left\lfloor\frac{2100}{2^4}\right\rfloor=131\ge75,\qquad
  \left\lfloor\frac{2100}{2^5}\right\rfloor=65<75,
  \]
  so \(v_2(c_{2026})=4\).

- For \(p=3\):
  \[
  \left\lfloor\frac{2100}{3^3}\right\rfloor=77\ge75,\qquad
  \left\lfloor\frac{2100}{3^4}\right\rfloor=25<75,
  \]
  so \(v_3(c_{2026})=3\).

- For \(p=5\):
  \[
  \left\lfloor\frac{2100}{5^2}\right\rfloor=84\ge75,\qquad
  \left\lfloor\frac{2100}{5^3}\right\rfloor=16<75,
  \]
  so \(v_5(c_{2026})=2\).

- For \(p=7,11,13,17,19,23\), we have \(\left\lfloor2100/p\right\rfloor\ge75\) but \(\left\lfloor2100/p^2\right\rfloor<75\), so each has exponent \(1\).

- For \(p\ge29\), \(\left\lfloor2100/p\right\rfloor\le72<75\), so the exponent is \(0\).

Thus

\[
c_{2026}=2^4\cdot 3^3\cdot 5^2\cdot 7\cdot 11\cdot 13\cdot 17\cdot 19\cdot 23.
\]

The number of positive divisors is

\[
(4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(1+1)^6
=5\cdot4\cdot3\cdot64
=3840.
\]

\[
\boxed{3840}
\]
